ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, US OFAC SDN list, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and New Zealand sanctions instruments adopted under the United Nations Act 1946. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified using the statutory definition in the AML/CFT Act 2009 and must be subjected to enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth/source of funds verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Adverse-media and sanctions screening must be repeated on a regular cycle, at minimum annually, and immediately upon any material ownership change.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_notes: New Zealand maintains a public register of directors and shareholders at the Companies Office, but no standalone public UBO register; beneficial-ownership information is collected and retained by reporting entities and is accessible to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, Financial Markets Authority, Department of Internal Affairs, and other AML/CFT supervisors on lawful request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Company Register via the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be constituted in Latin-alphabet characters; Te Reo Māori names and macrons are permitted; scripts other than Latin must be transliterated into Latin characters for register entry. Every company name must include the word 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation such as 'Ltd', and must be distinguishable from existing registered names and not misleading.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed for one further 20-working-day period upon payment of the current renewal fee prior to expiry. If the Companies Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request within 20 working days, stating why the name is not prohibited and does not create an undesirable similarity to an existing name under ss 20-22 of the Companies Act 1993. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand or, where applicable, pursue the statutory dispute process under the Companies Act 1993.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible in New Zealand only if it is a physical street address within New Zealand, is not a mere post-office box in law, and the provider is authorized to receive service of process and statutory notices. For a medium-risk video-chat social app, the AML/CFT and commercial-substance policy requires that the virtual arrangement be supported by board minutes, physical records, and a named registered agent able to produce corporate records upon request.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a fully digital company with no local staff or material physical assets; the likelihood increases to approximately 25% if the company later becomes an AML/CFT reporting entity, registers as a New Zealand financial service provider, or is identified as having high-risk destination or funding flows.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 2 (ss 8–22), ss 39–44 (share issues), ss 51–58 (directors), ss 122–134 (board resolutions), s 184 (delegation to officers), s 189 (director duties); Financial Reporting Act 2013 (financial reporting and disclosure); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (customer due diligence where obligations apply). The entity uses the commercial designation 'International Company' but is constituted as a New Zealand company limited by shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (Companies Act 1993, s 16) filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register together with consent notices and, where adopted, the constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked-capital requirement. The board may issue shares for consideration determined by the board, including no-par-value shares, and shares may be fully paid by cash, property, or other satisfaction permitted by the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY NAME] (COMPANY NO. [CN]) — RESOLVED, by unanimous written consent of all directors under s 122 of the Companies Act 1993, as follows: (1) SHARE CAPITAL: The allotment of [1,000] ordinary shares in the capital of the Company is approved, issued fully paid for consideration of NZ$[amount], and the subscribers named in the share register are recorded as shareholders. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company is adopted at [street address, city, New Zealand] and that address is confirmed as the registered office and address for service on the New Zealand Companies Register. (3) OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed as director, and [Name] is appointed as Chief Executive/company secretary with the authority conferred by the board and by law, including authority to file tax registrations and open bank accounts. (4) BANKING AND FINANCIAL CONTROLS: The opening of bank accounts with [authorised bank] is approved, and each authorized signatory's mandate is established. (5) TAX AND AML/CFT COMPLIANCE: The executive officers are directed to obtain an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number, register for GST where required, and implement the Company's anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism risk procedures consistent with the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Company's medium-risk enhanced due diligence profile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online portal (Companies Register; companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search against the Companies Register and Intellectual Property Office New Zealand (IPONZ) to ensure the proposed 'International Company' name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contain restricted words contrary to ss 14 and 15 of the Companies Act 1993. Submit an online name reservation if required. A name may be reserved for 20 working days with a possible extension notice.
required_dossiers: List of up to 3 proposed company names in order of preference
Certified identity evidence of each proposed director and shareholder
AML/CFT source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership questionnaire for the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar declines the name under s 14, the applicant may file written submissions and request reconsideration, or select an alternative name. If an opposition or objection is received from a third party, the applicant may withdraw and refile a new name, or apply to the High Court for judicial review of an unlawful refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of constitution and officer consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and New Zealand-licensed legal advisor; final record with the Companies Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, including share classes, director authority, quorum, shareholder decision rules, and indemnity provisions. If no constitution is adopted, the default rules in Schedule 2 of the Companies Act 1993 apply. Obtain executed consents to act as director from each proposed director pursuant to s 151, and validated official copies of identity documents and addresses for the share register and register of directors.
required_dossiers: Proposed constitution (optional but recommended for an international holding and IP structure)
Signed consent to act as director for each director
Certified passport or national identity card for each director and shareholder
Proof of residential or service address for each officer
AML/CFT beneficial-ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the constitution or consents are rejected, the Companies Office will issue a query notice. The applicant may correct the documentation and resubmit within the stated deadline. Any refusal based on a legal defect in the constitution may be cured by amending the constitution and re-executing consents before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online company incorporation application in the Companies Register. Enter the approved company name, registered office address, share structure, allotment particulars, director and shareholder details, and attach the constitution and consents. Validate the information, pay the prescribed filing fee by debit/credit card, and submit the application electronically. The application must be signed electronically or by a duly authorized presenting officer.
required_dossiers: Completed company incorporation electronic form
Adopted constitution, if any
Directors' signed consents
Registered office consent or authorisation of the registered office provider
Address for service
Share allotment and consideration details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried under s 17, the applicant may supply additional information or correct technical errors within the Registrar's deadline. If the application is finally refused, the applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review or submit a fresh application with amended particulars after curing the identified defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies – New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Office issues the Certificate of Incorporation and automatically allocates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Verify that the registered name, entity type, directors, shareholders, registered office, and authorised capital recorded in the electronic register are correct. Download and retain the certificate and the register extract for banking, tax, and commercial counterparty onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN registration record
Companies Register extract
Incorporation application reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or NZBN record contains a clerical or legal error, submit a request for correction through the Companies Register helpdesk or by filing a notice of change with the Registrar. A formal correction or cancellation and re-issue may be obtained under the Companies Act 1993 and the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, premises, and operations setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Fire and Emergency New Zealand, WorkSafe New Zealand, and local territorial authority building control
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NZBN to apply online for an IRD number through Inland Revenue. Register for GST if the company's annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is desired. If the company will hire employees, register as an employer for PAYE and related deductions. For the physical office or server room, obtain a building warrant of fitness, fire evacuation scheme approval, and Workplace Health and Safety risk assessment. Implement the first board resolution, issue the share certificates, maintain the shareholder register, and execute the banking mandate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
IRD number application or online registration
GST registration details
Employer registration details if hiring staff
First board resolution
Share certificates and shareholder consent
Bank account opening application with directors' certified IDs
Building warrant of fitness and fire evacuation scheme where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a penalty or registration query, the company may file a late-return remittance application under s 183 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. For premises clearance objections, the company may appeal the decision to the local territorial authority or District Court and remedy any identified compliance defects before re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) – Building System Performance branch; WorkSafe New Zealand; local territorial authority building control
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating licence is required in New Zealand for ISIC 6311 real-time video matching and information processing; standard business registration, Fire and Emergency New Zealand clearance, and building compliance for physical premises are the applicable formalities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from Full EIA – ISIC 6311 is not listed as a prohibited or controlled activity requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment under New Zealand law. If the company later operates a physical data centre or uses emergency generation plant, site-specific assessment may be required under the Resource Management Act 1991 through the relevant regional council.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions are generated by the core application activity. Any wastewater discharge to a municipal sewer must comply with the local territorial authority Trade Waste Bylaw and the Water Services Act 2021. Backup generator emissions, if installed, must meet the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004 for particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and volatile organic compounds. E-waste must be disposed of in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the New Zealand e-waste recycling guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) approval of the fire safety evacuation scheme and fire protection systems; annual building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004 for the occupied premises; structural load inspection certificate for any equipment installation; WorkSafe New Zealand health and safety policy, hazard register, worker training records, and accident/incident reporting protocol; Civil Defence Emergency Management business continuity plan under the Civil Defence Emergency Management Act 2002.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake) — New Zealand's national tax administrator; taxpayer portal is myIR (myIR.ird.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident or newly incorporated company that commences business activity in New Zealand must obtain an IRD number before filing income tax and/or GST returns. Procedure: (1) determine the form of entity and the activity to be conducted; (2) submit the applicable registration application — IRD Form IR596 (for non-resident individuals and special companies) or the online company registration via the New Zealand Companies Office and myIR for locally incorporated International Companies; (3) obtain an IRD number, which simultaneously serves as the GST identification number where GST registration is elected or required; (4) where trading turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 per 12-month period, complete GST registration on Form GST101A or through myIR; (5) submit supporting identity and corporate governance documentation (certificate of incorporation, director identification, registered office details, and foreign ownership details); (6) appoint a New Zealand tax agent or registered address for service if no local director is available. The IRD number issuance is generally completed within 5–10 business days of a complete application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box election; classification follows the Income Tax Act 2007 and applicable double-tax agreements. Available statutory elections include: (i) Look-Through Company (LTC) election for close-held companies to achieve fiscal transparency; (ii) Qualifying Company (QC) election with a separate entity-level rate; (iii) GST payment-basis election (invoice basis vs. payments basis) for cash-flow timing; (iv) GST grouping election under GST Act 1985; and (v) hybrid-mismatch election or consent-based arrangement adjustments under Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007 to neutralise deductible/non-inclusion mismatches for cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST — New Zealand Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (a broad-based VAT-type tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 annual turnover: a person must register for GST once supplies made in New Zealand in a 12-month period exceed or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000; supplies to non-residents outside NZ are disregarded for the registration threshold test.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control. Electronic invoice issuance is optional but increasingly standard; Inland Revenue supports voluntary Peppol (E-invoicing) interoperability for B2B and B2G transactions. GST-registered persons invoicing NZD 60,000 or more annually in a taxable activity must file GST returns and maintain electronic records; large businesses are expected to use myIR online lodgement, but there is no government approval or pre-clearance requirement for individual tax invoices. Tax records must be retained for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (a) goods physically removed from New Zealand by the supplier or recipient within 28 days of the time of supply; (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply where the services are not physically supplied to a person (or performed) in New Zealand and are not directly connected with real property situated in New Zealand; (c) international transportation and associated services; and (d) supplies of certain intellectual property rights and digital services to non-residents where the performance-based and land-based carve-outs do not apply. For the video-matching app scenario, the digital app services supplied to users outside NZ qualify for zero-rating where the offshore recipient is outside New Zealand and the services are not consumed in NZ; services consumed by individuals present in New Zealand remain standard-rated at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZ Customs Export Entry / Customs Export Declaration (approved export entry under the Customs and Excise Act 2018)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of goods from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer advice evidencing settlement from the offshore buyer
Executed supply contract with the non-resident customer including the non-resident status of the counter-party
Service delivery records/logs demonstrating that the services are performed offshore or supplied to a recipient outside New Zealand
Evidence of the non-resident’s jurisdiction of residence (e.g., foreign trade registry or tax certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating substantiation is subject to Inland Revenue audit under the Tax Administration Act 1994, with a four-year time bar (extendable for evasion or fraud). Wrongly claimed zero-rating may be clawed back with use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for unconscionable tax avoidance or abusive tax position, and up to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion or intentional misstatement. Offence-level penalties may also apply for knowingly creating false documentation in support of an export zero-rating claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) as the sole monetary authority, prudential regulator of registered banks, and operator of the ESAS real-time gross settlement system; jointly with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) exercising AML/CFT market-conduct supervision over financial service providers in New Zealand. For the CK_IC (a Cook Islands International Company), registration integrity is supervised by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission, and all NZD-denominated treasury clearing, foreign-exchange settlement, and bank prudential oversight flow through the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully free-floating and freely convertible currency under a deregulated financial system; since the March 1985 float there has been no exchange-control licensing regime, no capital-account approval queue, and no restriction on non-resident ownership of NZD or foreign-currency accounts. Current-account transactions (ISIC 6311 cross-border telephony and video-match subscription receivables) and capital-account transactions (equity injections, loans, and repatriation) are unrestricted, subject only to tax compliance, notably non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at 15% on dividends, interest, and royalties, treaty-reduced where a Double Tax Agreement applies, and to standard Balance of Payments statistical reporting by the receiving bank. The only material structural hurdle is the Overseas Investment Act 2005: a non-resident acquiring sensitive New Zealand land or significant business assets above the statutory thresholds (e.g., NZD 100M for non-OECD investors and NZD 200M for OECD investors) requires consent from the Overseas Investment Office; a treasury holding only bank deposits, trade receivables, and intellectual-property contracts will not trigger consent. For the tax-exempt CK_IC, the practical convertibility risk is bank de-risking rather than legal convertibility restriction; therefore, the treasury strategy must anchor on a Tier-1 New Zealand bank with a dedicated offshore-corporate client segment and a bilateral FX dealing line.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist in New Zealand. There is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export or service proceeds; the residual exchange-control powers of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand are emergency-only and are not exercisable in normal economic conditions. The CK_IC may lawfully retain 100% of its USD, Apple IAP, and Paymentwall receivables in foreign-currency settlement accounts, select the timing and counterparty for conversion into NZD, and maintain multi-currency balances as natural hedging. The only compliance incidents are (i) AML/CFT suspicious-transaction and large-cash reporting to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, (ii) the receiving bank's obligation to report the economic purpose of each inward credit to the RBNZ Balance of Payments survey using the BPM6 'computer services/information services' classification corresponding to ISIC 6311 / NAICS 519130, and (iii) daily transaction-monitoring obligations under the bank's customer risk-rating for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced profile.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (NZD/USD) plus Operational Multi-Currency Treasury Account with FX Direct dealing
Capital Escrow Account (NZD) plus Business Transaction Account with global FX hedging desk
Operational Account (NZD/USD dual-currency) with API-enabled bulk payment initiation
Operational Account (NZD) plus Corporate Money Market Account for short-term liquidity
Operational Account (retail-oriented; limited appetite for offshore tax-exempt corporate structures)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an auxiliary collection/payout rail, LOW as a primary treasury bank. New Zealand has no dedicated e-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime; a non-bank operator must register on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the FSP Act 2008, comply with the AML/CFT Act 2009 as a reporting entity, and cannot access the ESAS/NZClear settlement systems without a commercial-bank sponsor. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie, and Paymentwall Payouts can open business accounts for CK_IC and provide USD/EUR/GBP virtual ledgers, but the following legal constraints apply: (i) funds held with an EMI are not legal tender or protected deposits in New Zealand; (ii) EMIs generally decline tax-exempt offshore international companies without a substantive OECD nexus; (iii) sub-ledger positions at an EMI must be disclosed to the principal clearing bank, which will treat them as counterparty credit exposure; and (iv) direct consumer deposits into a NZ account would constitute unlawful deposit-taking outside the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989. Therefore, the CK_IC treasury architecture must use a Tier-1 New Zealand bank as the settlement anchor and EMIs only for niche purpose-specific rails such as rapid creator payouts in Southeast Asian markets.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible in New Zealand under the AML/CFT Act 2009, provided the bank completes acceptable electronic verification of directors and beneficial owners, including digital document validation, liveness checks, and independent source-of-funds corroboration. In practice, the Tier-1 banks will open accounts for CK_IC only under one of two routes: (i) an in-person 'new-to-bank' interview at a New Zealand branch conducted by at least one NZ-resident director or by a licensed NZ corporate-services trustee acting as agent; or (ii) a fully remote path requiring a video-conference interview with the ultimate beneficial owner, notarised board resolutions and a UBO certificate dated within three months, original banker's references from the directors' home banks, a Cook Islands registered-agent Certificate of Good Standing, and a registered address for service in New Zealand. If the IC will carry on business in New Zealand, it must also be registered as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993, and any NZ-resident director/agent must be an individual or licensed nominee. Without at least one of these nexus elements, expect refusal, a 90-plus-day compliance deferral, or the mandatory imposition of Enhanced Due Diligence for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced video-chat business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt Cook Islands International Company with no New Zealand economic substance, 100% foreign beneficial ownership, and no local payroll or tangible assets, requesting NZD/USD accounts at a Tier-1 New Zealand bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A consolidated corporate and substance bundle comprising: (a) Cook Islands Registrar of International Companies Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and registered-agent confirmation; (b) constitutional documents (Memorandum and Articles of Association) with a board resolution approving the New Zealand banking relationship; (c) a complete UBO declaration identifying all natural persons above 25% and their residential address, nationality, and source of wealth; (d) an economic-substance narrative demonstrating that CK_IC's treasury functions, share registry, and compliance oversight are administered by a licensed NZ trustee or corporate-services office, with a physical NZ address for service and an NZ-resident agent; (e) audited or management financial statements for the preceding two years; and (f) a group structure chart evidencing that the IC is the principal operating entity and not a layering vehicle. If substance is absent, the defense fails and the file must be remediated by appointing an NZ corporate-services administrator and registering as an overseas company before onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket micro-transactions from a real-time video-match social app funded through Apple IAP and Paymentwall, creating aggregate monthly flows of potentially millions of USD from digital-goods channels with elevated card-fraud, chargeback, and child-safety risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A merchant-integrity and platform-governance bundle comprising: (a) signed merchant-of-record agreements proving Apple (App Store IAP) and Paymentwall are responsible for consumer KYC, payment authorization, and chargeback management, and that CK_IC only receives net settlements; (b) a New Zealand-compliant AML/CFT programme including a business-wide risk assessment, customer risk rating methodology, transaction monitoring thresholds, and suspicious-activity escalation procedures; (c) PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance for any card data touchpoint; (d) robust KYC/age-verification and content-moderation policies for the random video-match service, including automated liveness/age checks, reporting protocols, and takedown mechanisms, evidencing that proceeds are not derived from unlawful content; (e) the app's privacy policy and Data Protection Impact Assessment under the Privacy Act 2020; (f) a three-month historical transaction summary showing average ticket size, geographic mix, refund/chargeback ratios, and settlement cycles; and (g) bank reference letters from the directors' home banks confirming legitimate source of personal wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic mismatch red flag: CK_IC is incorporated in the Cook Islands and banks in New Zealand, yet its users and counterparties span high-risk jurisdictions, and funds route through Singapore/HK/EMI sub-ledgers before landing in NZ, triggering correspondent-bank 'pass-through' money-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A jurisdiction-risk and funds-flow transparency bundle comprising: (a) a sanctions and adverse-media screening report (UN, OFAC, New Zealand consolidated sanctions, EU/UK lists) covering all UBOs, directors, counterparties, and the Paymentwall/Apple merchant configurations, generated by a recognised screening vendor; (b) a funds-flow map showing each origination channel (Apple IAP, Paymentwall card/wallet schemes), the settlement intermediary, the conversion point, and the final NZD/USD concentration account, with purpose codes on every leg; (c) transactional analytics evidencing IP-geolocation clustering, device-fingerprint integrity, and a demonstrable correlation between users and legitimate subscription/reward payments; (d) contractual chain proving CK_IC is principal in the service agreements and that no third party is acting as an unlicensed money remitter; (e) source-of-funds letters from each shareholder, together with six months of original bank statements supporting the capital injection; (f) board-attested declarations that no beneficial owner is a Politically Exposed Person, or the appropriate enhanced monitoring where a PEP is unavoidable; and (g) an undertaking to restrict transactions to/from sanctioned jurisdictions and to furnish quarterly independent AML/CFT audit reports to the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Founding and growth equity from non-resident shareholders or venture investors is injected via SWIFT MT103 from the remitter's bank to the CK_IC's ANZ or Westpac NZD/USD capital account. The remitter must complete the bank's inward-purpose declaration using the BPM6 classification 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital', and the receiving bank will file the corresponding Balance of Payments statistical return with the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. To avoid unavoidable-wealth flags, the IC must pre-approve each subscribing shareholder on its bank profile and attach: an executed board resolution allotting shares, an updated shareholders' register, the signed subscription agreement, and a funds-origin statement comprising six months of bank statements from the investor. If the investor is domiciled in a high-risk jurisdiction, the compliant routing is a two-hop transfer: first into the IC's Singapore/HK treasury collection account at a white-list bank, and second an onward MT103 carrying the full originator and beneficiary trail into New Zealand; the NZ clearing bank will require a narrative field stating 'Equity capital - no goods/services - ISIC 6311 video-match app' to prevent a trade-mismatch auto-suspend. No OIO consent is required while the injected capital is deployed as working capital, software-development spend, or financial assets; however, if the IC later acquires 25% or more of a New Zealand business above the Overseas Investment Act thresholds, the acquisition must receive OIO consent prior to settlement. USD tranches may be converted at the bank's dealing desk at interbank mid-minus-spread, with a booked forward where the deployment date is known and a swap where timing is uncertain.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The CK_IC treasury disburses along the following clearing rails: (1) Corporate payments via SWIFT MT103/MT202 for IP licensing, cloud-bandwidth, legal, accounting, and director fees, each tagged with an internal treasury reference (e.g., BANDWIDTH-AMZN-001) and backed by the underlying contract retained in the corporate treasury management ledger. (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) and documentary collections under URC 522 only where the IC is importing physical IT hardware, procuring server equipment, or acquiring intellectual property under a bank-assured escrow; for the core ISIC 6311 video-match service, an LC is not appropriate and repeated LC use without underlying transport documents would be a red flag, so the default is MT103. (3) Mass payout rails for revenue-share, content-moderation, developer, and influencer payments: the IC aggregates payouts through Paymentwall's payout API or through a file-based BNZ/ANZ bulk-credit product; NZD-denominated payouts clear via Payments NZ BECS (Bulk Electronic Clearing System) on a D+1 cycle, while foreign-currency payouts clear via SWIFT on a D+2 international cycle. (4) Intercompany funding movements between the NZ treasury account and the CK_IC's EMI sub-ledgers are executed as MT103 transfers with purpose code 'Intercompany loan - treasury centralisation' and are subject to automatic EDD prompts above NZD 10,000-equivalent. All outbound disbursements are screened against sanctions and adverse-media lists; beneficiaries showing aggregate flows above NZD 10,000-equivalent per rolling 30-day period trigger enhanced due diligence and contract verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (tenors up to 12 months) in NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR, and NZD/GBP, executed under ISDA/CSA or the bank's master FX terms, aligning with Apple's 21-day and 45-day App Store settlement cycles and Paymentwall's T+7/T+14 cycles to hedge subscription revenue repatriation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in PHP, VND, IDR, THB, INR, and BRL for collection proceeds from Southeast Asian and Latin American user cohorts that are ultimately settled in USD but expose the treasury to local-currency conversion variance.

Cross-currency swaps (XCS) converting a portion of the USD subscription float into NZD at matched tenors, funding the NZ-resident payroll, corporate-services administration, and cloud-hosting obligations without repetitive spot conversion.

Vanilla FX call and put options purchased from the ANZ/Westpac dealing desks, with capped premiums, to protect budget rates for strategic M&A or capex in foreign currencies, such as acquiring a 49% interest in a Philippine development studio or purchasing EU-based data-centre hardware.

Natural hedging through a multi-currency pooling and notional-pooling arrangement (e.g., ANZ Multi-Currency Account or Westpac Global Currency Account), allowing the IC to net USD, NZD, AUD, and EUR ledgers internally and to reduce the notional size and cost of outright derivative transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date—normally the anniversary of incorporation, or the approved alternative annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 200.00; if an annual return remains overdue for more than 6 months, the Registrar may issue a 20-working-day notice of intention to remove the company; non-compliance results in administrative strike-off and vesting of remaining property in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Directors' Statement (mandatory only for large companies and FMC/issuer reporting entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (registered filing with the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's balance date for the relevant accounting period; small exempt companies are not required to file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-filing contravention may result in court fines up to NZD 10,000 per director and continuing daily penalties, plus enforcement steps by the Registrar including deregistration of a persistently non-compliant company; filing is receipted without a separate fee.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to any company that is an issuer, an FMC reporting entity, or a 'large' company with total assets of at least NZD 60 million, total revenue of at least NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees; an audit must also be performed where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights give written notice requiring one. An exempt International Company that is below these thresholds and not carrying on business in New Zealand may remain unaudited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalent IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 and Tier 2 profit-oriented entities, issued by the External Reporting Board; Tier 3 and Tier 4 simplified accrual/cash accounting standards are available for smaller non-issuers. All statutory financial statements must comply with the Companies Act 1993 and present a true and fair view.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not require a separate standalone UBO annual filing. The annual return requires directors to confirm the current registered office, directors, and shareholder class information. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members before the transferee is recognised; if a transfer gives an individual 25% or more ownership/control, the Significant Controller Register must be updated within 10 working days. The Significant Controller Register must be kept at the registered office but is not filed annually with the Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including all share transfers and class details)
Register of Significant Controllers (25%+ ownership/control, where applicable)
Minute Book of shareholder and director meetings and resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450–1,200 per annum for a New Zealand registered office, resident agent/corporate secretary and registered document custody
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–6,000 for a voluntary exempt-company audit; USD 8,000–20,000 for a mandatory large-company IFRS audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The subject entity is classified as an International Company (CK_IC) in a Tax-Exempt Zone. A qualifying non-resident IC deriving no New Zealand-source income is effectively subject to a 0% New Zealand corporate tax rate, while a New Zealand-resident company is taxed at the statutory 28% rate. Available incentives include the New Zealand R&D tax credit of 15% on qualifying R&D expenditure, the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) concession of 2% on certain interest payments, and the IC regime exemption from New Zealand corporate tax where the entity is non-resident and does not carry on business in New Zealand.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Income Tax Return for Companies, filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR portal or an approved Gateway/MOVES software solution; the IR461 International Dealings Schedule is attached when cross-border related-party dealings exceed NZD 5 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due by 7 July following the fiscal year-end. For a non-standard balance date, filing is due no later than the 7th day of the 7th month after the balance date; approved tax agent extensions may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IRD number, balance date, accounting basis, and company tax code of the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IRD number should be that of the foreign company or its NZ branch; a non-resident IC should state its non-resident filing status and omit NZ resident company elections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate assessable income derived during the income year, including business income, dividends, interest, royalties, and attributable CFC income under New Zealand tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income that is New Zealand-sourced or attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment; wholly foreign-source income of a non-resident IC is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for expenses incurred in deriving assessable income, including employment costs, cloud infrastructure, marketing, depreciation, and arm's length transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses directly or proportionally related to the New Zealand-source income; related-party service and royalty expenses must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 21A – Taxable Income or Net Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income less allowable deductions and prior-year loss offsets, adjusted for tax legislation and imputation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC deriving no NZ-source income, enter nil; ensure the loss carryforward period is correctly applied and shareholder continuity rules are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax on taxable income at 28%, reduced by provisional tax already paid, resident withholding tax credits, imputation credits, and R&D tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies compute final tax only on NZ-source income and can claim foreign tax credits or treaty credits; an exempt IC will ordinarily show no tax payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty (LFP): NZD 250 immediately, plus NZD 50 per additional month of non-filing up to a maximum additional NZD 500. Late payment penalty (LPP): 1% of the unpaid tax on the due date, an additional 1% on the next 7th day, and 1% monthly thereafter. Use-of-money interest also accrues daily on unpaid tax at the prescribed rate, currently approximately 10.98% per annum.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR461 – International Dealings Schedule, filed electronically with the IR4 via myIR or approved software, required when the taxpayer has cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZD 5 million or forms part of a multinational group subject to Country-by-Country Reporting.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as IR4: 7 July for a 31 March balance date or 7th day of the 7th month after a non-standard balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A – Jurisdictions of Associated Enterprises
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of each foreign associated enterprise jurisdiction and the relationship between the parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an IC video-chat app, disclose the country of the app developer, payment processors, and group IP holder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate amounts for related-party sales, purchases, services, interest, royalties, and other dealings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Apple IAP and Paymentwall commission flows if such payment processors are connected to an associated enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the transfer pricing methodology applied to each transaction category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split methodology was used and why.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts of any voluntary transfer pricing adjustments made in the New Zealand tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must adjust for any economic rent shifted to low-tax related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation has been prepared and retained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Documentation must be available to Inland Revenue upon request within 30 days; failure to maintain it is a separate reporting offence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing of IR461 attracts the NZD 250 late filing penalty, a 20% shortfall penalty for unacceptable tax position, and may escalate to a 100% abusive tax position penalty where documentation is deliberately suppressed. Intentional omission can be recharacterised as evasion and prosecuted criminally.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory NRWT on dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company to non-resident shareholders. The rate may be reduced to 15% for fully imputed dividends under domestic rules and further reduced under applicable DTAs, e.g. 15% under the OECD/NZ standard treaty, 5% where the recipient is a company holding at least 10% of the voting power, and 0% in certain jurisdictions for 80%+ corporate owners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the recipient must be the beneficial owner, resident in a DTA jurisdiction, and must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of that jurisdiction. The non-resident must submit Form IR372 (NRWT reduced-rate declaration/certificate of residence) to the New Zealand payer before any payment is made. The payer reviews the certificate, performs a back-to-back arrangement check, and applies the reduced treaty rate at source. If over-withheld, the recipient must file a New Zealand income tax return to claim a refund within the statutory four-year period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT is 15%, generally reduced to 5% under most New Zealand double tax agreements where the beneficial owner is entitled; some treaties provide 10%. Interest: statutory NRWT is 15%, commonly reduced to 10% or 0% under DTA treaties; the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply in lieu of NRWT for qualifying public-listed New Zealand corporate debt paid to non-associated non-resident lenders.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 5,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for the income year, triggering the IR461 schedule and required contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue above NZD 1,300,000,000.
